qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Various pairs of loosely coupled dislocations connected by an APB are distinguished in both the dark field and weak beam images; dislocations can initiate or terminate APBI faults when arranged in pairs (superdislocations of the underlying B2 lattice) or as four-coupled dislocations (superdislocations of the DO3 lattice). Even though loosely coupled by weak APB faults, they largely glide and behave as individual (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations.

Examination using +g and −g imaging conditions shows that many pairs are loose superdislocation partials (marked p), while others are loose dipole pairs (marked d), similar to those seen in Fe–20% Al except that the segments tend to remain more straight and close to the screw orientation.

slip_behavior.value: Deformation occurs by the movement of single (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations; because the APB energies are too low, superdislocations do not form and the dislocations appear completely dissociated as single dislocations trailing the corresponding APB fault. Dislocations remain straight and in near-screw orientations.

phase_evolution.value: During slow cooling the DO3-ordered Fe–25% Al develops coarse B2 domains with thermal APBs and fine DO3 domains or some partial disorder, since the composition is close to where two-phase disorder + DO3 order co-exist; APBI faults are generated by dislocation movement during deformation.

interface_notes.value: The APB energies for both APBI and APBII faults are insufficiently high to retain the dislocations together as closely coupled superdislocations in this DO3-ordered alloy (APBI energy is so low that dislocations appear completely dissociated).

unmapped_findings: For the DO3-ordered Fe–25% Al alloy the APBI energy is so low that dislocations appear completely dissociated as single (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations trailing the corresponding APB fault; superdislocations do not form in this material and single dislocations trail shear APB (b0052, b0063).

DO3 order in the Fe–25% Al alloy is imperfect; its composition is close to that where two-phase disorder + DO3 order co-exist, and the fine dark-field background speckling (Fig. 8) may be due to fine DO3 domains or the formation of some disorder (b0034).

The Fe–25% Al alloy (DO3 ordered) maintains a relatively low work hardening rate because its APB energies are not high enough to keep dislocations coupled as superdislocations, so the stronger superdislocation-dipole hardening mechanism does not operate (b0057, b0063).
